intention: The library room + the LEARN verb (cairn/devices/librarian/library.py). The library: a room in instance-space at the ratified address ~/.cairn/devices/librarian/0/library/ — a shelf of FROZEN copies with stable citable addresses. The register (_manifest.json) freezes each file's digest at shelving; re-shelving same content writes nothing; DIFFERENT content at a standing address is refused loudly — an address must not rot, because provenance anchors point INTO it. The graph stays the catalog (the embedding is the path; retrieval is a walk, never a shelf scan). LEARN is deposit-only — 'densify the graph, no artifact': every passage of a shelved file embeds and deposits through the same provenance gate as everything else, anchored {source: library:<address>, passage: p<n>, sha256: <frozen digest>}, cited by RAW paragraph position so filtering never renumbers a neighbor.
why: Akien, verbatim (held-librarian, 2026-07-27): 'my suggestion is that the librarian also have A LIBRARY. In .cairn --- it can hold the various files we'll be rereading from in TheIgorsProject... Dewey decimal system or some other organization... i dunno. whatever will work.' The organization that works: shallow stable shelving + graph-as-catalog — what the shelves must supply is not taxonomy but STABLE CITABLE ADDRESSES, since a node says 'this came from shelf X, passage Y' and that address must not rot. LEARN is the first of his three request verbs (learn / learn+summarize / learn+summarize-by-X-time) and the 'learning always' half of the chatbot face.
traces_to: Law 1 — re-shelving and re-learning both write nothing; the graph already holds the frozen file and the register's digest guarantees it is the SAME file
Law 3 — learned nodes are hypotheses at birth like everything else; the citation carries the frozen digest so the claim is checkable against the shelf
Law 5 — the citation shares an address with what it cites: shelf + passage + digest travel IN the node's provenance, and the register lives IN the room
Law 7 — rot is loud: an unshelved, missing, drifted, or binary source refuses BEFORE any deposit; a rotted address fails its citations rather than quietly grounding new ones
Law 8 — a hollow shelf (mutable addresses, unregistered copies, renumbering citations) cannot pass the teeth
